ota.summary: # TubesZB 2026.10.29.1 This prerelease introduces a custom TubesZB web interface and one firmware per hardware model with saved DHCP/static IPv4 settings. ## Replacement for the failed 2026.10.29.0 build This prerelease supersedes [2026.10.29.0](https://github.com/tube0013/TubesZB-ESPHome-Builder/releases/tag/2026.10.29.0). ## Important upgrade information **An existing firmware with a compiled-in static IP starts on DHCP on its first upgrade to this firmware.** The old compiled address is not present in the new settings storage. Find the device's DHCP lease in your router, or try its existing hostname. Open **Network**, enter the desired static settings, apply them, then open the new address and select **Keep settings** within two minutes. Update the connection address in ZHA, Zigbee2MQTT or Z-Wave JS if it changed. Once confirmed, network settings survive normal restarts and OTA updates.. An unconfirmed network trial automatically restores the previous configuration after 120 seconds or an unexpected reboot. Use the image for your exact hardware model. Use `.ota.bin` for a device OTA update and `.factory.bin` for a serial/USB installation with https://web.esphome.io. Devices that have not previously been updated with ESP-IDF-based firmware may require a serial/USB update. ## New TubesZB interface The main device URL now opens a custom TubesZB web ui with desktop/mobile layouts and light/dark appearance. The interface is embedded in the firmware and does not require an internet connection. - **Overview:** device identity, network and radio connection status. - **Zigbee / Z-Wave:** the controls and status supported by each radio, with independent sections on dual-radio hardware and a link from Zigbee to radio firmware controls. - **Network:** DHCP/static IPv4 configuration, validation of addresses and subnet settings, confirmation/rollback, and the saved **Use without internet** option. - **Firmware:** gateway and radio firmware management together, local OTA uploads, confirmation dialogs, progress at the top of the page and short completion messages. - **Diagnostics and logs:** a log dropdown on every section except Overview. Capture and history persist across navigation; returning to Overview hides the panel without discarding captured logs. Logs are buffered in the browser. Logs can now be downloaded as text. The original ESPHome interface remains at `/esphome` for compatibility. ## Saved network settings and offline use Static entries are validated before saving, including IPv4 syntax, subnet mask and device/gateway consistency. An IP configuration change the device will reboot, and you must actively acknowledge that the new settings work within 2 minutes or the previous settings will be restored. **Use without internet** If you wish to keep your device off the internet, you can disable all internet checks for firmware updates now. re-enabling internet access will trigger an immediate check. ## Radio firmware and controls - Zigbee firmware manifests may specify an application `baudrate`. After a successful transfer, the flasher applies it ensuring the new firmware is able to communicate before re-enabling the serial stream. Failed transfers or missing metadata retain the previous rate; the bootloader's rate remains separate. A direct `.gbl` URL has no manifest baud metadata, so use the matching application baud when changing firmware that way. - All firmware flashes now have a progress bar during the update, to follow along with more information enable the logging. ## Hardware coverage The release builds 22 hardware profiles: | Family | Profiles | | --- | --- | | Single-radio CC2652 | CC2652P2 Ethernet/USB and PoE 2021–2023; CC2652P7 PoE 2023 | | Single-radio Silicon Labs | MGM24; MGM210 PoE 2022/2023; retired MGM12 Pro1 and original MGM210 Series 2 | | Dual-radio | CC2652 + Z-Wave, MGM24 + Z-Wave and MGM21 + Z-Wave, including their experimental entries | | Z-Wave | Original and 2026 Z-Wave profiles, including experimental entries | Newly enabled older-board flashing and MGM21 software entry still need physical-device verification. Earlier owner testing covered Z-Wave OTA/network rollback, CC2652 flash ownership, MGM24 + Z-Wave behavior, and BM24 forward/reverse baud migration between 115200 / 7.4.4.0 and 460800 / 9.1.2.1. These reports do not replace a final hardware pass for this version. **Changes:** [Builder PR #200](https://github.com/tube0013/TubesZB-ESPHome-Builder/pull/200) · [Component PR #7](https://github.com/tube0013/esphome-components/pull/7) · [Compare with 2026.10.25.0](https://github.com/tube0013/TubesZB-ESPHome-Builder/compare/2026.10.25.0...2026.10.29.1)
